To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

undernutrition in women of childbearing age, during pregnancy, and in children younger than 2 years of ages contributes to 1*3 million child deaths per year and that maternal overweight and obesity and childhood overweight and obesity have become important contributors to adult obesity, cardiovascular disease, and diabetes.

in 2011, maternal undernutrition and overweight and child undernutrition were the cause of 1*1 million deaths of women of reproductive age and 2*1 million child and infant deaths, and that these conditions were also responsible for 3*1 billion disability adjusted life years (DALYs) lost in 2011 and 2012, and that the burden of disease caused by malnutrition is likely to rise in the coming years.

in 2011, maternal undernutrition and overweight, together with childhood undernutrition, were responsible for 35% of deaths in children younger than 2 years, 11% of deaths in women of reproductive ages, and 10% of deaths in men.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of interventions to improve maternal nutrition and child nutrition, and to reduce the burden of disease in low income and low and middle income countries.
the causes of malnutrition and its consequences in women of reproductive ages, pregnancy and children in the early years of life.
the development of the child, the health of the child, and the development of the adult.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
malnutrition, in all its forms, is an underlying cause of death and disability in low income and in middle income countries, and a major contributor to the global burden of disease.

maternal and child undernutrition in low income countries is a major contributor to child mortality and to adult non communicable diseases and that maternal overweight and obesity are important contributors to maternal morbidity and child mortality.
maternal undernutrition and childhood undernutrition and overweight are important public health problems that are amenable to prevention and treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the burden of malnutrition is high in low income and some middle income countries and has not decreased as rapidly as expected.
maternal and child undernutrition is a major cause of child deaths and that maternal overweight and obesity is a growing problem.
the global prevalence of maternal undernutrition and child stunting has decreased during the last decade.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the burden of undernutrition in the world is much greater than is commonly thought and that the burden of maternal and child undernutrition in the first 1000 days of life is much larger than the burden of maternal overweight, which is itself a growing problem.

undernutrition in women and children in low income and lower middle income countries is a major cause of child and maternal morbidity and mortality, and that overweight is a major cause in women of reproductive ages.
undernutrition and overweight are major causes of disease and death in low income and some middle income countries and that these conditions are largely preventable.
